clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old woman with a 20-pack-year smoking history presented with a persistent cough for 3 months. Chest CT identified a 10 mm nodule in the right upper lobe with supraclavicular, mediastinal, and right hilar lymphadenopathy. Mediastinoscopy confirmed adenocarcinoma with EGFR mutations, and brain MRI revealed metastases, establishing stage IV disease. She was treated with carboplatin, pemetrexed, and bevacizumab triplet therapy, achieving partial response. However, drug-induced interstitial pneumonia developed, necessitating treatment discontinuation. Two weeks after pneumonia onset, she developed prominent oedema and erythema in the neck and face, followed by dyspnoea. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe SVC stenosis. A skin biopsy of the erythematic site demonstrated neoplastic cells within the lumina of dermal lymphatic vessels with infiltration into the dermis and hypodermis, with immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin, TTF-1, and napsin A, confirming lymphangitic carcinomatosis. The patient died of respiratory failure 1 week after CLC diagnosis.
